?Court No. - 50
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 5290 of 2022
Appellant :- Sachin

Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Appellant :- Sunil Kumar Yadav
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Janmed Kumar Hon'ble Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra,J.
Heard Sri Sunil Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri Janmed Kumar learned counsel for the first informant, learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.

Instant criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of SC/ST (P.A.) Act has been filed against the order dated 12.7.2022 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Etah in Bail Application No.1894 of 2022, (Sachin vs. State of U.P.), arising out of Case Crime No.37 of 2022, under Sections 376, 506 IPC & Sections 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (PA) Act, Police Station- Sakit, District- Etah.

According to the prosecution version, the FIR was lodged at the instance of prosecutrix on 7.4.2022 at 13:32 hours, wherein she stated that on 5.3.2022 at about 6:00 P.M., when she had gone to ease herself alone at the outskirt of the village in a field, the accused met and held her hand.
He pointed a countrymade tamancha at her temple and forcefully made her lying on the earth and committed rape on her.
On hearing her shrieks, the witnesses Rinku and Jaipal, who were returning from the fields, had appeared and the accused made her good escape on noticing them.
The husband and father-in-law of the victim came to the place of accused to make a complaint but they were threatened by accused side.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the FIR in present case has been lodged after more than one month of the incident, which gives ample scope to embellish the prosecution version.
The accused appellant has been falsely implicated in the case due to village partybandi on account of last Gram Pradhan Election.

He further submitted that even the witnesses Jaipal and Rinku had stated in their statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. that they had seen the accused fleeing away from the place of incident and subsequently, they came to know that the accused committed rape on victim.
They have not seen the actual incident and from perusal of their statement, it cannot be inferred that they have seen the actual incident.

He further submitted that the victim in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has improved her version and stated that the accused had threatened her at the time of incident by giving threat to her as well as her little child, who was present there.
Her husband was in Delhi on that date and when she informed him about the incident, he rushed to his home on next date.
However, she has also stated that due to intervention of village pradhan, her FIR was not lodged by police promptly.
The victim stated that she was 4 months pregnant at the time of incident and now of eight months at the time of her medico legal examination, which took place on 18.6.2022.
However, the Doctor has noticed no mark of injury on her person externally or internally.
He next submitted that the appellant is in jail since 6.6.2022.
He undertakes to be abide by conditions of bail.
He lastly submitted that the learned court below has rejected the bail application of the appellant on insufficient grounds.
The case of the appellant for the purpose of bail was not duly considered by learned court below.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the informant

has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant and submitted that the prosecution version is natural and the victim was subjected to rape by appellant in the field and the independent witnesses have also seen that the accused was fleeing away from the place of occurrence.
Learned counsel for the informant further submitted that the family members of the accused are threatening the victim, therefore, the appellant may not be enlarged on bail.

Considering the arguments advanced on behalf of the parties, facts and circumstances of the case,
nature of the offence, long incarceration of the appellant in jail but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
Accordingly, the appeal is hereby allowed.
The impugned order dated 12.7.2022 rejecting the bail application of the appellant is hereby set aside.

Let the appellant- Sachin be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) That the appellant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.

(ii) That the appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the Sachin vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157451626/

sentences.text: (iii) That after his release, the appellant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
(iv) The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned before the release of the appellant on bail.
(v) The appellant will report to police station concerned on second and fourth Sunday of each month in the day hours until recording of the statement of the victim before the Court.
It is made clear that in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the appellant.

It is also made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
